title: Amortized requantization pipeline for attention KV and prefill
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Dequant/requant overhead during prefill is a dominant contributor to per-request latency for INT8/FP8 mixed-precision paths when using large KV caches. Current implementation performs eager dequant on every prefill chunk and requant on each kernel input, which amplifies memory bandwidth and CUDA kernel launch costs for streaming and large-batch prefill workloads.

Goal: Design and implement an amortized requantization pipeline that reduces per-token dequant/requant work by (a) performing coarse-grained dequantization once per cache tile, (b) reusing a compact "staged" FP32/FP16 intermediate in GPU memory for multiple decode steps, and (c) integrating tiled fused-attention kernels that accept a hybrid view (INT8 weights + staged FP16 activations) to avoid frequent cast/repack. Target improvements: reduce prefill p95 latency by >=15% for long context loads and reduce GPU memory traffic attributed to dequant by >=25%.

Constraints: Must preserve numerical parity within acceptable SNR for customer workloads (bleu/qa/llm-eval regressions <= small tolerance), remain compatible with existing model variants, and support safe fallbacks to existing dequant path on correctness or hardware incompatibility. Implementation should be toggleable via runtime feature flags and expose telemetry for per-path token cost and latency breakdowns.
acceptance_criteria: New staged dequant buffer implemented and integrated with KV prefill; toggleable via feature flag
Fused tiled attention kernels accept hybrid INT8 weight + staged FP16 activations without full per-token requant
Benchmarks: prefill p95 reduced by >=15% on gpus-standard-8 for sequence lengths >=4096; dequant memory traffic reduced by >=25%
Automated regression suite shows no statistically significant degradation on representative eval prompts (toplevel evals linked)
Telemetry exposes per-request dequant/requant time and bytes moved; rollout gated on metrics
notes: 2026-02-12: Initial spike showed ~28% of prefill GPU memcpy time attributed to per-chunk dequant on int8 models (small testbed with gpus-standard-8)
2026-02-18: Design review with ML infra, serving runtime, and ops. Decided to pursue staged FP16 buffer rather than full FP32 to save memory and leverage existing fp16 fused kernels.

2026-02-22: Trade-off: staged FP16 reduces numerical headroom vs FP32 but allows use of half-accumulate kernels; agreed to add stricter eval gating and a 'full-precision' fallback path for sensitive customers.

2026-02-28: Prototype kernels merged to experimental branch: tile_fused_attn_hybrid_v1; microbenchmarks show 12% lower launch overhead and 20% less bandwidth for the attention forward compared to baseline on 2048 context.

2026-03-05: Found regression on some fp8-model configs at extreme seq len due to accumulation saturation; mitigated by selective fp32 accumulation on critical matrix multiplications (configurable per-layer).

2026-03-09: Integration tests running in canary on internal prod cluster; no customer-facing errors but small increase in decode jitter for a small subset of prompts (investigating prompt sensitivity).
2026-03-12: PR (see links) updated to add runtime flag 'amortized_requant.enabled' and telemetry counters 'dequant_bytes','requant_ops','staged_buffer_hits'.
perf_results: gpus-standard-8, model-X-int8, seq=4096: baseline p95 prefill=320ms -> amortized path p95=265ms (17% improvement)
gpus-standard-8, model-Y-fp8, seq=2048: bandwidth attributed to dequant reduced from 42GB/s -> 30GB/s (28% reduction)
cost projection: token GPU-time reduced ~9% for long-context batch workloads
next_steps: Finish canary rollout targeting 2 internal services (Apr-03 window) and collect A/B metrics
Add layer-level accumulation config to safely enable fp16 accumulation where stable; expose as 'accum_mode' in model profile
Extend unit tests to cover cross-device staged buffer eviction and verification of numeric parity within tolerance
Prepare runbook for rollback if parity regressions observed in production; include automated metric checks
